Secondary conversational sense ('other forms:  (gen/acc),  (dat),  (instr),  (prep)') used in spoken Russian dialogue.
+ infinitive: Пора идти = Time to go

examples.trans: It's time for us to go.

meanings.note: ничего не осталось = there's nothing left

examples.text: Ну что, очкарик? Видишь, ничего не осталось.

meanings.note: + instrumental; со before some consonant clusters: со всеми

examples.trans: Share it all equally with everyone, understand?

Secondary conversational sense ('still, yet') used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.trans: But you've still got some. Give me just one.

meanings.note: Russian preposition meaning 'on' that governs a specific oblique case on the following noun phrase.
Secondary conversational sense ('onto, to; for') (+ accusative: на второй срок) used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.trans: The programme is on the website.
He is running for a second term.

examples.trans: I love our town very much. That's why I'm running for a second term.

meanings.note: agrees in gender and case with the noun

meanings.note: Common feminine noun meaning 'minute' in everyday Russian.

examples.trans: I'll be there in ten minutes.

examples.text: Ладно, будь там. Через десять минут буду.
examples.trans: All right, stay there. I'll be there in ten minutes.

meanings.note: goes right before the word it negates

Russian imperfective verb expressing ongoing, habitual, or repeated action meaning 'can', forming an aspectual pair with 'смочь'; conjugates for person and number in the present/future and agrees in gender in the past tense.

examples.text: Этого не может быть. Это наша история.
examples.trans: That can't be. It's our history.

meanings.note: Invariable Russian adverb used to modify verbs or whole clauses with the sense 'very'.
Secondary conversational sense ('very much') (with verbs: очень люблю) used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.trans: I love our town very much.

examples.text: Я очень люблю наш город. Поэтому я иду на второй срок.
examples.trans: I love our town very much. That's why I'm running for a second term.

meanings.note: Manner or predicative adverb in '-о' derived from the corresponding adjective stem, used in everyday speech to mean 'strongly'.

examples.trans: The wind is blowing hard outside.

examples.text: Я так два года потеряла. Любила так сильно!
examples.trans: I lost two years like that. I loved him so much!

спешить.gloss: to hurry, be in a rush

meanings.en: to hurry, rush, be in a hurry
meanings.note: куда ты спешишь? = where are you rushing to?

examples.trans: What happened? Where are you rushing to?
We are in a big hurry for the train.
Wait a bit, Sokolov. Do not hurry.

meanings.note: Russian preposition meaning 'at' that governs a specific oblique case on the following noun phrase.
Secondary conversational sense ('I have') (possession) used in spoken Russian dialogue.
Secondary conversational sense ('from (ask from someone)') (просить у кого) used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.text: Привет! Смотри, что у меня есть.

meanings.note: Invariable Russian adverb used to modify verbs or whole clauses with the sense 'again'.

examples.text: Нина, не слушай. Это опять обман.
examples.trans: Nina, don't listen. It's another trick.

meanings.note: Manner or predicative adverb in '-о' derived from the corresponding adjective stem, used in everyday speech to mean 'a lot'.
Secondary conversational sense ('more') (comparative) used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.text: Мы сделали много, но надо сделать ещё больше.
examples.trans: We've done a lot, but we need to do even more.

meanings.note: Adjective formed with the common Slavic suffix '-н-' from a noun/verb root. Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('important').

examples.text: Я тебе утром говорил: не торопись. Это очень важный вопрос.
examples.trans: I told you this morning: don't rush. It's a very important question.

meanings.note: Declinable neuter noun meaning 'matter', changing its case ending across all six Russian grammatical cases to mark its role in the clause.
Secondary conversational sense ('matter, business') used in spoken Russian dialogue.
Secondary conversational sense ('case (in court)') used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.trans: I have a lot to do.

examples.text: Мне некогда об этом думать. Слишком много дел.
examples.trans: I have no time to think about that. There's too much to do.

meanings.en: must, need to, it is necessary
meanings.note: Manner or predicative adverb in '-о' derived from the corresponding adjective stem, used in everyday speech to mean 'it is necessary'.

examples.trans: We need to do even more.

meanings.note: Prefix 'за-' marks beginning an action, covering, or stopping by along the way (stem 'ехать'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'drop by, stop in'.

examples.text: Надо заехать домой, принять душ, переодеться.
examples.trans: I need to stop by home, take a shower, change.

examples.text: Надо заехать домой, принять душ и переодеться.
examples.trans: I need to stop by home, take a shower, and change clothes.

examples.text: Можешь по дороге заехать на рынок за свежей зеленью?
examples.trans: Can you drop by the market for fresh herbs on the way?

meanings.note: Invariable Russian adverb used to modify verbs or whole clauses with the sense 'home'.

examples.text: А ты иди домой и делай уроки.
examples.trans: And you go home and do your homework.

examples.text: Так, мы идём к слепым. А ты иди домой и делай уроки.
examples.trans: Right, we're going to the blind people. And you go home and do your homework.

принять.gloss: to receive, to see (a visitor); to accept

meanings.note: Prefix 'при-' indicates approaching, attachment, or slight degree of action (stem 'нять'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to receive, to see (a visitor); to accept', paired with 'принимать'.
Secondary conversational sense ('to accept, to take') used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.trans: You recognised me. Thanks for seeing me.

meanings.en: shower (bathroom apparatus or act of washing)
meanings.note: Common masculine noun meaning 'shower' in everyday Russian.

examples.text: Они выложили фотографию прямо из душа.
examples.trans: They posted a photo straight from the shower.

examples.text: Пока ты не сходишь в душ.
examples.trans: Before you go take a shower.

meanings.note: Prefix 'пере-' denotes crossing over, repeating, or exceeding a limit (stem 'одеться'). Reflexive/intransitive verb with the postfix '-ся'/'-сь' (historically from the reflexive pronoun 'себя', oneself). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'change clothes'.

examples.text: Надо заехать домой, принять душ, переодеться.
examples.trans: I need to stop by home, take a shower, change.

examples.text: Надо быстро заехать домой, принять душ и переодеться.
examples.trans: I need to quickly stop by home, take a shower, and change clothes.

examples.text: Повара должны переодеться в чистую форму перед началом смены.
examples.trans: The cooks must change into a clean uniform before the start of the shift.

meanings.note: Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'лушать'). Used in Russian as an imperfective verb expressing ongoing, habitual, or repeated action meaning 'to listen', forming an aspectual pair with 'послушать'.
the imperative 'слушай' starts a sentence, like 'look, ...'
Secondary conversational sense ('hello (on the phone)') ('Слушаю' = I'm listening) used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.text: Слушай, Самсон, я тут подумал. Твой начальник — такой опытный специалист.
examples.trans: Listen, Samson, I've been thinking. Your boss is such an experienced specialist.

надоесть.gloss: to bore, to get on someone's nerves

meanings.note: the person who is fed up is in the dative: 'мне надоело' = I'm fed up
Secondary conversational sense ('' + infinitive' = I'm tired of doing ...') used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.text: Надоело мне в этом архиве сидеть.
examples.trans: I'm tired of sitting in this archive.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian pronoun ('what') whose case form reflects its grammatical role in the clause.
Secondary conversational sense ('that') (conjunction) used in spoken Russian dialogue.
Secondary conversational sense ('? = well?') used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.text: Привет! Смотри, что у меня есть.

meanings.note: вот именно = that's just it, quite right
Secondary conversational sense ('namely') (а именно = namely) used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.text: Именно это я и хотел сказать.
examples.trans: That is justamente what I wanted to say.

examples.text: Вот именно. Но мне сдаваться нельзя.
examples.trans: Exactly. But I must not give up.

meanings.note: + infinitive; agrees with the subject: должна (f)
Secondary conversational sense ('owe') used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.text: Жадность, Паша, должна быть умеренная. Комнатной температуры.
examples.trans: Greed, Pasha, should be moderate. Room temperature.

meanings.note: the present tense is normally left out: я мэр = I am the mayor
Secondary conversational sense ('there is, there are') (present есть; у меня есть = I have) used in spoken Russian dialogue.
future: буду / будешь ... + infinitive

examples.trans: You will be asking for forgiveness.

meanings.note: Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'пать'). Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to sleep', paired with 'поспать'.

examples.text: Ладно, утром позвоню ей. Поехали спать.
examples.trans: All right, I'll call her in the morning. Let's go to sleep.

meanings.note: Invariable Russian adverb used to modify verbs or whole clauses with the sense 'here'.

принимать.gloss: to receive, to see (visitors); to take

Secondary conversational sense ('to take, to accept') used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.trans: The mayor isn't seeing anyone today.

examples.text: Я ему сказала, что сегодня вы не принимаете.
examples.trans: I told him you're not seeing anyone today.

meanings.en: far, far away, a long way
meanings.note: Manner or predicative adverb in '-о' derived from the corresponding adjective stem, used in everyday speech to mean 'far'.

examples.text: Насколько далеко зашло всё это следствие?
examples.trans: How far has this whole investigation gone?

meanings.note: Invariable Russian adverb used to modify verbs or whole clauses with the sense 'from here'.

examples.text: Я выйду отсюда через две недели. Я решу все ваши проблемы.
examples.trans: I'll be out of here in two weeks. I'll solve all your problems.

meanings.note: emphatic at the start of a sentence
Secondary conversational sense ('? = really?, oh yeah?') (disbelief) used in spoken Russian dialogue.
pointing at a thing or a situation; 'это' + noun = 'this is ...'
points at something: это моё = that's mine
Secondary conversational sense ('is') (linking word: главное — это народ) used in spoken Russian dialogue.
Secondary conversational sense ('other forms:') used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.trans: And this is for you. A toy car!

meanings.note: Prefix 'за-' marks beginning an action, covering, or stopping by along the way (stem 'нимать'). Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'occupy, take up'.

examples.text: Да, это занимает очень много моего времени.
examples.trans: Yes, it takes a lot of my time.

meanings.note: Russian determiner/pronoun ('my') agreeing in gender, number, and case with the noun phrase it specifies.
Declinable neuter noun meaning 'time', changing its case ending across all six Russian grammatical cases to mark its role in the clause.

examples.text: Я и сама хорошо проведу время.
examples.trans: I'll have a good time on my own.

meanings.note: Invariable Russian adverb used to modify verbs or whole clauses with the sense 'then'.
Secondary conversational sense ('then, in that case') used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.text: Я тебе тогда сказал: ты меня ещё поцелуешь.
examples.trans: I told you back then: you'll kiss me one day.

meanings.note: Invariable Russian adverb used to modify verbs or whole clauses with the sense 'what for'.

examples.trans: Hi, Arkady Borisovich. What are you doing?

meanings.note: Descriptive Russian adjective meaning 'every', agreeing in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies.

examples.text: Аркаш, мне москвичи звонят каждый день. Может, всё-таки передумаем?
examples.trans: Arkasha, the people from Moscow call me every day. Maybe we should reconsider after all?

meanings.note: на днях = in the next few days, or the other day

examples.trans: I'll call in the next few days.
Any day now, on the website.

meanings.note: Invariable Russian adverb used to modify verbs or whole clauses with the sense 'that's why'.
Secondary conversational sense ('that's why') (потому и = that's exactly why) used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.text: Я устал, потому что много работал.
examples.trans: I'm tired because I worked a lot.
I'm at home because I'm ill.

meanings.note: там такие деньги = there's so much money in it

examples.trans: Hello! How was it in Hungary?

meanings.en: to lie, to be lying down, to rest
meanings.note: Russian imperfective verb expressing ongoing, habitual, or repeated action meaning 'to lie', forming an aspectual pair with 'полежать'; conjugates for person and number in the present/future and agrees in gender in the past tense.

examples.text: Такие люди должны лежать в особенном месте!
examples.trans: Such people should lie in a special place!
The book is lying on the table.
But I'll be lying next to Grishka for eternity.

meanings.note: Russian determiner/pronoun ('all') agreeing in gender, number, and case with the noun phrase it specifies.
Secondary conversational sense ('everything') (neuter всё) used in spoken Russian dialogue.
Secondary conversational sense ('everyone') (plural все) used in spoken Russian dialogue.

Secondary conversational sense ('things, belongings') (plural 'вещи') used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.trans: There's someone here to see you.

examples.text: Аркадий Борисович, извините, тут к вам человек.
examples.trans: Arkady Borisovich, I'm sorry, there's a man here to see you.

переехать.gloss: to move (to a new home or city)

meanings.note: Prefix 'пере-' denotes crossing over, repeating, or exceeding a limit (stem 'ехать'). Used in Russian as an perfective verb focusing on a single completed action or result meaning 'to move', forming an aspectual pair with 'переезжать'.

examples.trans: They moved into a new flat.

examples.text: Ты в Москву переехала, да? Поедем сейчас в сауну, посидим!
examples.trans: You moved to Moscow, right? Let's go to a sauna now and sit for a while!
